Gift Guide

The Best Shawls for Wedding Gifting

What to give, what to spend, and why ivory outlasts every other choice. A practical guide to gifting handwoven textiles at Indian weddings.

Pashmore Editorial·30 April 2026·6 min read

A shawl is one of the few wedding presents that is still in use twenty years later. It is also one of the easiest to get wrong, because the obvious choices — bright colours, heavy embroidery — are the ones that date fastest.

For the bride

Crimson and deep burgundy are traditional for bridal kani, and a full-field kani shawl is the most significant textile gift that exists in this part of the world. If the budget is not there, an ivory Pashmina with a tilla border does the same job: it reads as ceremonial without competing with the outfit.

Shop the pieceCrimson Bridal Kani Shawl

For the groom

A plain charcoal or midnight Pashmina shawl, cut to men’s proportions, worn over a bandhgala. Undecorated is the point — it will be worn at every winter wedding for the rest of his life, which an embroidered piece will not.

For the families

Matched sets solve the hardest problem in wedding gifting, which is giving to two people at once without giving them the same thing. A shawl and stole dyed in a single bath read as a pair without being identical.

What to spend

  • Close family: ₹25,000 and above — kani, full sozni, or a numbered piece.
  • Extended family and close friends: ₹10,000–20,000 — pure Pashmina, tilla border or plain.
  • Colleagues and wider circle: ₹5,000–10,000 — a boxed Pashmina stole or a fine wool shawl.
  • Volume gifting: speak to a gifting desk rather than buying retail; most houses box and dispatch individually.

Three rules

  • Choose ivory or a deep neutral when in doubt. It never dates and it suits everyone.
  • Insist on presentation — the box, the sleeve and the certificate are half the gift.
  • Include the craft certificate. Knowing who made it is what turns a purchase into an heirloom.
